name: GaPP2
aliases: Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women
question: Does gabapentin improve worst or average pain compared with placebo in women with chronic pelvic pain and no obvious pelvic pathology?

design.blinding: double-blind; participants, clinicians and research staff masked
design.population: Women aged 18–50 years with pelvic pain for at least 3 months and no obvious pelvic pathology on laparoscopy within the preceding 36 months.
design.locator: PMC7527829 Methods, Study design and participants; Results, trial profile

verdictNote: Neither coprimary pain outcome met the prespecified significance threshold.
takeaway: In women with chronic pelvic pain and no obvious pathology on laparoscopy, gabapentin did not significantly improve worst or average pain versus matching placebo at weeks 13–16; serious adverse events were more frequent with gabapentin.

reports.label: 16-week randomized comparison
reports.citation: Horne AW, Vincent K, Hewitt CA, et al. "Gabapentin for chronic pelvic pain in women (GaPP2): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *Lancet.* 2020;396(10255):909-917. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(20)31693-7
reports.followUp: Coprimary pain assessment at weeks 13–16; treatment through week 16.

results.measure: Adjusted mean difference in change from baseline to weeks 13–16 on a 0–10 numerical rating scale
results.note: 97.5% CI; two-sided alpha 0.025 for each coprimary endpoint; planned minimum important difference 1 point. End-of-study scores were 7.1 and 7.4. Difference adjusted for baseline score and minimisation variables.
results.locator: PMC7527829 Results, Table 2, Worst NRS pain score; Statistical analysis

results.measure: Adjusted mean difference in change from baseline to weeks 13–16 on a 0–10 numerical rating scale
results.note: 97.5% CI; two-sided alpha 0.025 for each coprimary endpoint; planned minimum important difference 1 point. End-of-study scores were 4.3 and 4.5. Difference adjusted for baseline score and minimisation variables.
results.locator: PMC7527829 Results, Table 2, Average NRS pain score; Statistical analysis

results.endpoint: At least 30% reduction in worst pain
results.measure: Women with at least 30% improvement from baseline at week 16
results.note: 99% CI; secondary outcomes were not assigned formal P values.
results.locator: PMC7527829 Results, Table 3, Reduction in NRS score from baseline

results.measure: Very marked or marked improvement at weeks 16–17
results.locator: PMC7527829 Results, Table 3, Patient global impression of change

harms.label: Serious adverse event
harms.note: P=0.04; one death from pneumonia complications in the gabapentin group was judged unrelated to study participation.

harms.label: Visual disturbances
harms.note: Risk ratio 2.25 (99% CI 0.99–5.10); P=0.01 as reported.

delivery.label: Study sites
delivery.locator: PMC7527829 Methods, Study design and participants

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: Oral gabapentin or matching placebo daily for 16 weeks; 300 mg starting dose, increased by 300 mg every 3 days during a 4-week titration to pain relief or tolerance, to a maximum of 2700 mg/day.

delivery.label: Available coprimary outcome data
delivery.note: Combined follow-up: worst pain 246/306 (80%); average pain 244/306 (80%).

delivery.label: Self-reported adherence
delivery.value: Adherence meant taking more than half of assigned doses; the reports were not validated with pill counts.
delivery.locator: PMC7527829 Results, Adherence paragraph; Methods, Outcomes
